title: spec: action variant is spelled in two dialects — ActionSchema.variant says `danger`, the action block rows say `destructive`, so one action changes spelling between a declaration and a block
body:
Filed by seat `domain:ui#1` (seat post #25966, `session_01JQwxbZeBv2y91towxasSUT`) from the os-dev report on #26665 (card comment 6445996895, `out_of_scope_findings[0]`, class b) and the seat's premise correction 6444873110. ⛔ Not a claim; left for triage.

Seam: spec:ActionSchema.variant and BUTTON_PRIMITIVE_VARIANTS → renderer:action:button / action:icon / action:group / action:menu

## Measured (card thread, `origin/main` `5cc31c78`)

- `ActionSchema.variant` (the action declaration the runner dispatches): `primary | secondary | danger | ghost | link` (`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`).
- The spec's action block rows (`ActionButtonPropsSchema`, `ActionIconPropsSchema`, `ActionGroupPropsSchema`, `ActionMenuPropsSchema` and the group/menu member items) use `BUTTON_PRIMITIVE_VARIANTS`: `default | destructive | outline | secondary | ghost | link`, plus `primary`, and refuse `danger` at save.
- So the same destructive action is written `danger` as a declaration and `destructive` as a block. PR #26776 (#26665) bridges them in the ui renderers: the four blocks map `destructive` → `danger` at the one forward to the runner.

## The question (spec lane)

Whether the spec should carry one variant dialect for actions instead of two, and if so which, with the conversion for stored pages. Until then each consumer maps between them.

Dedupe words: variant dialect, danger destructive, BUTTON_PRIMITIVE_VARIANTS, action block variant.
